# Weekly Updates

Every student in the Lab sends a written end-of-week update to the person they report to,
with `strategy-program@byu.edu` in CC.

That is the whole mechanism, and it is accountability all the way up the chain. A club VP
reports to their co-presidents. Those co-presidents report to Soraya. The program
co-presidents report to Scott. Nobody reports into a void, and nobody is left guessing what
the people below them did this week.

The CC does two things: it gives the Strategy Program one place to track completion, and it
means your leader is never the only person who knows you did the work.

directly to Lena Lizunova.

### If you hold two roles

Some leaders serve in two places at once, for example a program VP who is also a club VP.
Your choice how to handle it:

- **One email** addressed to both leaders, with the body split by role so each of them can
  find their part, or
- **Two separate emails**, one to each leader, each covering only that role.

Either way it counts as one update for the week. CC `strategy-program@byu.edu` on whatever
you send. If your two roles sit in different tiers, use the later of the two deadlines.

If you receive updates from people below you, read them before you write your own. Your
update should reflect what your team did, not only what you personally touched.

## Deadline

Two deadlines, because the updates cascade. VPs write first so their co-presidents have
something to roll up.

| You are | Due | Covers |
|---|---|---|
| VPs | **Friday, 11:59 PM** | The week just finished, including that day's session |
| Presidencies | **Monday, 11:59 PM** | Your own week plus what your VPs reported |

Friday night for VPs is hours after class, while what you committed to in the Practice block
is still fresh. Many people write it in the twenty minutes after the session ends.

Monday for presidencies gives you a full weekend gap to read five or six updates and write
one that speaks for the club. It also means Soraya, Lena, and Scott start the week with eight
summaries rather than 27 scattered emails, with the whole week ahead to unblock anything
flagged.

Nothing here requires working on a Saturday or a Sunday.

- First VP update: Fri, Sep 11. First presidency roll-up: Mon, Sep 14.
- Last VP update: Fri, Dec 4. Last presidency roll-up: Mon, Dec 7.
- No update the week of Thanksgiving. There is no class Nov 27.
- There is no class Oct 16, but an update is still due that week.
- Total: 12 each.

Session 1 on Sep 4 is the kickoff, so no update follows it.

## Format

Three sections, the same ones used in the APM Lab internship. Keep it to one screen.

**1. What I did this week [Required]**

- Completed events, meetings, outreach, and deliverables
- Lead with outcomes, not activity. "42 students at the case workshop" beats "held a case
  workshop."
- Include numbers when you have them: attendance, applications, offers, signups

**2. What I am doing next week [Required]**

- Priorities and planned work, with dates
- Be realistic about what fits in a week

**3. Blockers, risks, or dependencies [Omit if none]**

- Anything that might slow you down
- What you need from your leader or another team
- Decisions you are waiting on

### One extra section for club leaders

Club co-presidents add a fourth section, because their updates are what
the Friday Announcements block is built from.

**4. What students should know [Required for club leaders]**

- Upcoming events with dates, deadlines, and how to participate
- Written for a student who is not in your club and may not be a strategy major. Spell out
  acronyms and say what the event is for.
- Write it so it can be read aloud in class on Friday without editing.

## Example

```
Subject: PMA Weekly Update - [Name] - Week of Sep 8

Hi Soraya,

What I did this week:
- Ran the PM resume workshop, 38 students attended, 22 from outside the strategy major
- Confirmed Adobe for the Oct 2 info session
- Sent 14 alumni outreach emails, 6 replies so far

Next week:
- Finalize the fall mentorship pairings (Maya owns this)
- Post the case competition signup form
- First mock interview round, Thursday evening

Blockers:
- Still need a room for Oct 2, the request has been pending two weeks
- Our marketing VP is out for a family emergency through the 20th

What students should know:
- PMA is hosting an Adobe info session Thu, Oct 2 at 5:00 PM in the Tanner Building.
  Open to any major. No signup required.
- Mentorship applications close Fri, Sep 19. Anyone interested in product management
  can apply, first or fourth year, any major.

Thanks,
[Name]
```

A VP update is shorter. Three sections, often five or six bullets total.

## Grading

Twelve updates, graded individually. The category weight is on the
[Assessments](00-assessments.qmd) page.

| You are | Full credit | Half credit through | No credit |
|---|---|---|---|
| VPs | Fri, 11:59 PM | Mon, 11:59 PM | After Monday |
| Presidencies | Mon, 11:59 PM | Wed, 11:59 PM | After Wednesday |

Each late window closes at the point the update stops being useful. A VP update that arrives
after Monday night missed the roll-up it was meant to feed. A presidency update that arrives
after Wednesday leaves nobody time to act on a blocker before the week ends.

Missing the CC means the update cannot be tracked, and an untracked update does not count.
Add `strategy-program@byu.edu` to your contacts in week one.

## What Makes a Good Update

- **Short.** Bullets, not paragraphs. If it runs past one screen, cut it.
- **Specific.** Numbers, names, dates. "Good turnout" tells your leader nothing.
- **Honest about blockers.** Flagging a problem early is the entire point. A clean update
  every week from a team that is struggling is worse than no update at all.
- **Consistent.** The value is in the streak. Twelve on-time updates build a record of the
  semester that nobody has to reconstruct in December.
